keyVerseText: The sons of Shemaiah; Othni, and Rephael, and Obed, Elzabad, whose brethren were strong men, Elihu, and Semachiah.
rootMeaning: The root of סְמַכְיָהוּ (Semachiah) is סָמַךְ (çâmak), which means to bear up, sustain, or support, combined with יָהּ (Yah), a shortened form of the divine name Jehovah. Literally, the name means "Jehovah has sustained" or "supported by Yahweh." This etymology emphasizes divine support and strength, going beyond a mere label to convey a profound reliance on God's sustaining power.
usageInScripture: The name סְמַכְיָהוּ appears only once in Scripture, specifically in 1 Chronicles 26:7, where it is translated simply as "Semachiah." The consistent rendering as a proper name highlights its identity as an individual, specifically a Korahite Levite. Though limited in occurrence, its translation maintains the connection to the meaning of divine sustenance embedded in the name.
theologicalSignificance: The name Semachiah reminds believers that their strength and endurance come from God Himself. In the biblical context, names often reveal character or divine interaction, and here the meaning "Jehovah has sustained" points to the faithfulness of God in upholding His people. For the Christian faith, this underscores the truth that all our support and perseverance are rooted in Christ, who sustains us continually. It invites a posture of trust and dependence on God’s sustaining grace in every circumstance.
keyVerseReflection: In 1 Chronicles 26:7, Semachiah is listed among the sons of Shemaiah, described as strong men. The presence of Semachiah, whose name means "Jehovah has sustained," enriches this portrayal by suggesting that their strength is not merely physical but divinely upheld. This verse subtly points to the source of their might and reliability as coming from God’s sustaining power, encouraging readers to recognize God’s hand in the strength of His servants.
